newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car sales slide 33.6 percent in January.
newsitem.headline: French car sales slide 33.6 percent in January.

text.p: New car sales in France fell 33.6 percent in January from year-earlier levels, the French carmakers association CCFA said on Monday.
"This sharp drop confirms the trend observed since November 1996 when the effects of the expiry of the (state rebate programme) Prime Qualite began to be felt," the CCFA said in a statement.

It said January 1997 had the same number of working days as January 1996, but that the year-earlier period was marked by a spurt in sales following the disruption caused by public transport strikes during December 1995.

New car sales, in provisional volume terms, totalled 122,552 last month, compared with 184,541 in January 1996. A CCFA spokesman said January 1996 car sales were probably inflated by 20,000 units due to the spillover from December orders.
Demand in January 1996 was also underpinned by a year-long new-cars-for-old rebate programme that expired at the end of September.
PSA Peugeot Citroen sales were down 43 percent, while Renault SA sales fell 29.3 percent.
The French carmakers held 53.4 percent of the market in January, compared with 55.7 percent in January 1996.
